falsifiers: packages/core/src/scheduler/__falsifiers__/inv-sch-<nn>.json, one per id. `falsifiers.test.ts` fails if an owned id has no file, if a file names an id that is not owned, or if the test a file names does not exist.

requests.what: Merge the `owned` array above into docs/invariants-owned.json. Every id already has a green owning test on this branch; the coverage map simply cannot see them from here.

EC-SCH-11 calls `max_new_items_per_local_day = 40` and `min_hours_between_introduction_and_production = 4` SHARED constants, and the economy config is the one table. They are currently declared as `DEFAULT_SCHEDULER_ECONOMY` in packages/core/src/scheduler/config.ts, injected through a `SchedulerEconomy` parameter that every call site already takes. Move the two values into the economy table and delete `DEFAULT_SCHEDULER_ECONOMY`; no call site changes.

`ItemId` and `SessionId` are re-declared in packages/core/src/scheduler/types.ts with the SAME brand strings, because the shared type surface had not landed on origin/main when this branch was cut. Identical brands are structurally identical, so replacing those declarations with a re-export is a no-op. Do it rather than leaving two spellings.

`spendDailyRefreshItem` keeps its own `spentItemIds` list. INV-SCH-05's spent-marker must be ONE marker shared by both surfaces, which is `ReviewPoolDay.spentBy` in packages/core/src/scheduler/pool.ts. Have the daily-refresh helper delegate to `serveItemsFromPool`, or the two lists will drift and the invariant becomes true in each file and false in the app.

`startOfLocalDay(day, zone)` — the inverse of `localDayOf`, used by the 7-local-day report window — lives in packages/core/src/scheduler/holds.ts because `day/` is another task's lane. It is day arithmetic; move it there.

`localDayOf` constructs a fresh `Intl.DateTimeFormat` on every call. Measured 2026-09-11 on this Mac: 200,000 calls take 5,706 ms that way against 115 ms with one formatter reused per zone — 28 us per call against 0.6 us, a factor of 50. It is on the render path (every streak chip, every quest countdown, every day-keyed rule) and it dominates every zone-keyed property in the suite, this task's included. Cache one formatter per `timeZone` in a module-level Map; the function stays pure.

notes: INV-SCH-01's median clause is asserted over histories with NO LAPSE. A lapse (`Again`) legitimately shortens the interval — that is what forgetting means — and asserting otherwise would require the scheduler to hide a real memory event. The guard's own clause (an early review changes nothing) is asserted over every history, lapses included. Measured 2026-09-11: with the guard removed, non-lapse histories produce up to 28 outright interval decreases and a median decrease in roughly one history in four hundred, so the clause is falsifiable rather than decorative.

INV-SCH-02's `honest-clock bound` is proved, not estimated. An analytic ceiling (the same grade at maximum elapsed) is WRONG: stability is not monotone in elapsed across states and grades, and `[Easy, Again]` falsified it at 8.2956 against a computed ceiling of 3.9056. The property instead constructs the monotone, non-negative clock sequence that reproduces the adversarial state exactly.
